lore_summary.en: The last Achaemenid. Pride before the Greek tide. A king who would not bend, and so is broken.
lore_summary.fa: دارا تخت را از پدرش داراب به ارث برد. اسکندر از غرب آمد با روش‌هایی که قرن‌ها کارگر نبودند. دارا شکست خورد. وزرایش خودشان کشتندش. اسکندر گریان سرش را نگه داشت — و برادرِ ناتنیِ او بود. آخرین خواسته: روشنک را به زنی بگیر.

scenes.body_en: Dara inherited the throne from his father Darab and everything that came with it — the long memory of Iran's greatness, the weight of the Kayanian line, the certainty that had served every king in the chronicle until it stopped serving them. He was a capable king and a proud one. The Shahnameh does not present him as weak. It presents him as a man who could not adjust to a world that was changing faster than any king had yet seen.
scenes.body_fa: دارا از پدرش داراب تخت را به ارث برد و همه آنچه با آن می‌آمد — خاطره طولانی عظمت ایران، بار نسب کیانی، قطعیتی که تا آنگاه به هر شاه در روایت خدمت کرده بود. پادشاهی توانمند بود و مغرور. شاهنامه او را ضعیف نشان نمی‌دهد. او را به عنوان مردی نشان می‌دهد که نتوانست خود را با دنیایی که سریع‌تر از هر آنچه تا به حال دیده بود در حال تغییر بود، سازگار کند.

scenes.body_en: The Greek campaigns were already in motion when Dara took the throne. A young commander named Sekandar had been moving east with an army that seemed to follow different rules. He moved faster, improvised more, treated supply lines as suggestions. His army was already at the border of what had been Persian territory. Dara sent the customary communications — tribute demands, warnings, the formal language that had always preceded either negotiation or war. Sekandar returned them with courteous rejection. The army kept moving.
scenes.body_fa: وقتی دارا به تخت رسید، لشکرکشی‌های یونانی از پیش در جریان بودند. فرمانده جوانی به نام سکندر با ارتشی که به نظر می‌رسید از قوانین متفاوتی پیروی می‌کند، از شرق حرکت می‌کرد. سریع‌تر حرکت می‌کرد، بیشتر اصلاح می‌کرد، خطوط تامین را پیشنهاد می‌گرفت. ارتشش از پیش در مرز آنچه قلمرو ایرانی بوده بود. دارا مکاتبات معمول را فرستاد — درخواست‌های خراج، هشدارها، زبان رسمی‌ای که همیشه پیش از مذاکره یا جنگ می‌آمد. سکندر آنها را با رد مودبانه برگرداند. ارتش به حرکت ادامه داد.

scenes.body_en:
The battles came. The Shahnameh describes them not as defeats of weakness but as defeats of mismatch — a king who fought with methods that had worked for two centuries against a commander who had developed something new, and the new thing won. After the final battle, Dara's own ministers stabbed him rather than be captured with him. He was found dying by a roadside.

Sekandar found him there. What happened next is the Shahnameh's most unexpected moment in this chapter: Sekandar wept. He held Dara's head. He promised to avenge the ministers who had killed him. And then the revelation — Sekandar was Dara's half-brother. Both were sons of Darab: Sekandar through the Greek princess Nahid whom Darab had divorced, Dara through his Persian queen. Two half-brothers who met only when one was dying and the other was weeping over him.

Dara's last request was that Sekandar marry his daughter Roshanak and protect the dynasty's continuity. Sekandar agreed, and kept the agreement. What Dara could not protect with his army he protected with his dying request — the bloodline continued through the marriage, the Kayanian line persisted through the loss, and the chronicle could move forward into the new age that had just arrived.
scenes.body_fa:
نبردها آمدند. شاهنامه آنها را نه به عنوان شکست‌های ضعف بلکه به عنوان شکست‌های عدم تطابق توصیف می‌کند — شاهی که با روش‌هایی می‌جنگید که دو قرن کار کرده بودند در برابر فرمانده‌ای که چیز جدیدی توسعه داده بود، و چیز جدید پیروز شد. پس از نبرد نهایی، وزیران خود دارا را کشتند تا همراه او دستگیر نشوند. در حال احتضار در کنار جاده یافت شد.

سکندر آنجا او را یافت. آنچه پس از آن اتفاق افتاد غیرمنتظره‌ترین لحظه شاهنامه در این فصل است: سکندر گریست. سر دارا را گرفت. وعده داد از وزیرانی که او را کشته بودند انتقام بگیرد. و سپس وحی — سکندر برادر ناتنی دارا بود. هر دو پسران داراب بودند: سکندر از شاهزاده خانم یونانی ناهید که داراب طلاقش داده بود، دارا از ملکه ایرانی‌اش. دو برادر ناتنی که فقط وقتی یکی در حال مردن و دیگری در حال گریه کردن بر او بودند، دیدار کردند.

آخرین درخواست دارا این بود که سکندر با دخترش روشنک ازدواج کند و پیوستگی سلسله را حفظ کند. سکندر موافقت کرد، و به توافق عمل کرد. آنچه دارا با ارتشش نتوانست حفظ کند، با درخواست محتضرانه‌اش حفظ کرد — نسب از طریق ازدواج ادامه یافت، خط کیانی از طریق باخت باقی ماند، و روایت توانست به دوران جدیدی که تازه رسیده بود وارد شود.

battle.intro_en: Dara refused to bend. The Shahnameh records his pride without apology and his defeat without contempt. To face this gate you must hold both truths at once.
battle.intro_fa: دارا از خم شدن سر باز زد. شاهنامه غرورش را بدون عذرخواهی و شکستش را بدون تحقیر ثبت می‌کند. برای مواجهه با این دروازه باید هر دو حقیقت را باهم نگه داری.

battle.intro_tg: Доро аз хам шудан саркашӣ кард. Шоҳнома ғурури ӯро бе узрхоҳӣ ва шикасташро бе таҳқир сабт мекунад. Барои рӯбарӯ шудан бо ин дарвоза бояд ҳар ду ҳақиқатро якҷо нигоҳ дорӣ.

codex.summary_en: Dara refused to negotiate with Alexander from a position of weakness. The Shahnameh records this without judging it: his pride is presented as a real quality, not a flaw. He was the descendant of Darab, the heir of four centuries of Achaemenid rule, and the legitimate king of an empire that had been larger than Alexander's at its height. His refusal to bend to the Greek tide was not vanity — it was a accurate assessment of what he was and what bending would mean. The Shahnameh does not pretend pride is always wrong. Sometimes it is the only appropriate response.
codex.summary_fa: داراب از مذاکره با اسکندر از موضعِ ضعف سر باز زد. شاهنامه این را بدونِ قضاوت ثبت می‌کند: غرورش به عنوانِ ویژگیِ واقعی ارائه می‌شود، نه عیب. شاهنامه وانمود نمی‌کند غرور همیشه اشتباه است.

codex.summary_en: The Shahnameh records Dara's defeat without contempt. This is significant: in a chronicle written in the Iranian tradition about an Iranian king's defeat by a foreign conqueror, the temptation to find moral fault in the defeated king would have been strong and politically useful. Ferdowsi resists it. Dara lost not because he was morally inferior but because the structural conditions — exhausted empire, superior Macedonian tactics, Dara's betrayal by his own commanders — produced a defeat. The moral quality of the king and the outcome of the battle are separate things.
codex.summary_fa: شاهنامه شکستِ دارا را بدونِ تحقیر ثبت می‌کند. فردوسی در سراشیبیِ پیدا کردنِ عیبِ اخلاقی در شاهِ مغلوب مقاومت می‌کند. کیفیتِ اخلاقیِ شاه و نتیجه‌ی نبرد از هم جداست.

codex.title_en: Dara Betrayed by His Own Commanders
codex.summary_en: Dara is killed not in battle but by his own commanders — Bessus and Nabarzanes — who saw the defeat coming and tried to bargain their way to Alexander's favour by removing the man they served. The Shahnameh records this betrayal with characteristic precision: the failure of Dara's reign is not his military defeat, which might have been recoverable, but the betrayal by the men whose loyalty was the foundation of his power. When that loyalty dissolved, the empire dissolved with it. The battle was the symptom. The betrayal was the disease.
codex.summary_fa: دارا در نبرد کشته نمی‌شود بلکه توسطِ سردارانِ خودش — که معامله‌ی خود را با اسکندر می‌خواستند — خیانت می‌بیند. شکستِ نظامی شاید قابلِ جبران بود. خیانت نبود.

codex.title_fa: نگه داشتنِ هر دو حقیقت به طورِ همزمان
codex.summary_en: The Shahnameh asks its reader to hold Dara's pride without apology and his defeat without contempt simultaneously. This is the harder reading. The easy readings are: Dara's pride caused his defeat (moralistic) or Dara was a victim of superior force (apologetic). Neither of these is what the Shahnameh says. What it says is: he was proud in a way that was appropriate to who he was, and he was defeated by forces that had nothing to do with his moral quality. Both things are true. The reader who can hold both understands what the Shahnameh means by a ruler's tragedy.
codex.summary_fa: شاهنامه از خواننده می‌خواهد هم غرورِ دارا بدونِ عذرخواهی و هم شکستش بدونِ تحقیر را همزمان نگه دارد. این خواندنِ سخت‌تر است. هر دو چیز درست هستند.

codex.summary_en: Alexander finds Dara dying — betrayed by his own men, abandoned by his army. He holds him, and the Shahnameh says he wept. Whether or not this is historically accurate, it is narratively precise: the conqueror weeping over the conquered is the Shahnameh's image of what a civilized person does when they encounter the full weight of what they have done. The weeping does not undo the conquest. But it establishes that Alexander was not indifferent to it, and that distinction — between the conqueror who cares and the conqueror who does not — is the Shahnameh's moral minimum.
codex.summary_fa: اسکندر دارا را در حالِ مرگ می‌یابد. او را نگه می‌دارد و شاهنامه می‌گوید گریست. فاتحِ گریان فتح را پس نمی‌گیرد — اما ثابت می‌کند که نسبت به آن بی‌تفاوت نبود.

codex.title_en: The End of the Achaemenid World
codex.summary_en: Dara's death ends the Achaemenid dynasty in the Shahnameh's chronology. What follows — the Arsacid period — is a different political structure, a different form of Iranian rule. The Shahnameh marks this transition without ceremony because the ceremony would be false: Dara does not die as the last representative of a noble tradition. He dies as a betrayed king in a ditch, killed by his own men. The Shahnameh is honest enough to record this without making it into a heroic last stand. The world that ended with Dara ended badly, and that is how the Shahnameh records it.
codex.summary_fa: مرگِ دارا سلسله‌ی هخامنشی را در گاه‌شماریِ شاهنامه پایان می‌دهد. شاهنامه این گذار را بدونِ تشریفات ثبت می‌کند — چون تشریفات دروغ می‌بود. دنیایی که با دارا پایان یافت بد پایان یافت.
